title: NASA-UAP-D023, Interview Excerpt with Astronaut Gordon Cooper, 1962
what_is_it: An auto-transcribed excerpt of a 1962 television interview, in which a journalist questions an astronaut about unidentified flying objects and the possibility of extraterrestrial life.
core_summary: In this interview excerpt, the astronaut says a large number of well-qualified people have seen objects with no logical explanation, though he allows each sighting may individually have one. He speculates that among the thousands of possible other planets with a livable atmosphere, some might host human-type life, and that some of these objects could conceivably originate there. He also notes that Mercury flights only reach about a hundred miles up, far too low to make observations on this question, and touches on the 'snowflakes'/'fireflies' seen from capsules.
interpretation_warnings: Auto-transcribed audio — names are garbled (e.g. 'Sharon Carpenter' likely the astronauts Schirra/Carpenter; 'something of this time' may be a mis-transcription).
The astronaut's remarks are personal opinion and speculation, not evidence or official findings.
Single-source excerpt of a longer 1962 interview; surrounding context is missing.
Speaker explicitly allows that each sighting may have a conventional explanation, so this is not a claim of proven extraterrestrial objects.

The record is one speaker's personal opinion from a single interview, not evidence or an official finding.
